title: 6 Best GoHighLevel Alternatives in 2026 (Honest Comparison)
desc: The best GoHighLevel alternatives in 2026 compared: HubSpot, ActiveCampaign, Systeme.io, Keap, Vendasta and ClickFunnels, with every price re-verified July 2026.
keywords: best gohighlevel alternatives, gohighlevel alternatives 2026, gohighlevel competitors, alternatives to gohighlevel, gohighlevel vs hubspot, gohighlevel vs vendasta
cta: Not sure which platform is right for your business?
body:
Quick answer: the best GoHighLevel alternative depends on what you actually need. Want polish and deep reporting without reselling software? Look at HubSpot. Mostly need email and marketing automation? ActiveCampaign is leaner and cheaper. Solo creators are better served by Systeme.io, which has a real free plan. Small service businesses that want hands-on onboarding should weigh Keap. Agencies that prefer reselling a marketplace of done-for-you products can compare Vendasta, and funnel-first marketers can look at ClickFunnels. That said, if your goal is to run an agency and resell one rebranded platform, GoHighLevel is still hard to beat, and we explain exactly when below.

We build and run GoHighLevel for agencies every week, so this is not a drive-by listicle. Below is an honest map of the six alternatives worth your time in 2026, what each one costs, and the catch nobody puts in the headline. Every price here was re-checked against the vendor's own pricing page on July 28, 2026, and two of our June figures were wrong. We have corrected them in the open rather than quietly editing them out.

Why people look for a GoHighLevel alternative

GoHighLevel is the default all-in-one for marketing agencies in 2026, with three plans: Starter at $97 per month, Unlimited at $297 per month, and the Pro or SaaS Mode plan at $497 per month that lets you rebrand and resell the platform as your own software. It is powerful, but there are three honest reasons people shop around:

  • The learning curve is real. GoHighLevel does a dozen jobs (CRM, funnels, email, SMS, calendars, automation, reputation, courses), and that breadth takes weeks to master. If you only need one or two of those jobs, it can feel like overkill.
  • Usage is billed on top of the plan. Email, SMS, and phone run through a usage wallet that sits on top of your monthly fee, so a small agency often spends another $100 to $200 per month once campaigns are live. HighLevel now also publishes a full add-on menu, and the useful ones add up: AI Employee at $50 or $97 per sub-account, a branded client portal app at $49, online listings at $30, premium prospecting at $29 and SEO at $79, all per sub-account, plus the white-label mobile app at $497 a month. The sticker price is not the full price.
  • It is built for agencies, not solo users. If you are a single business or a course creator, you are paying for resale and multi-client features you will never switch on.

If none of those apply to you, GoHighLevel is probably still your best option, and you can start a free 14-day GoHighLevel trial here. If one or more do apply, here are the alternatives that make sense.

The alternatives at a glance

Here is the short version before we go deep. Starting prices are the entry paid tier on annual billing where a vendor offers one, all verified on the vendor's own pricing page on July 28, 2026. Where monthly billing costs materially more, we say so in the section below.

What changed since we published this

This guide went live on June 15, 2026 and every platform was re-verified on July 28. Two of our figures were wrong, one vendor rebuilt its pricing model, and two held exactly. The detail sits in each section below; here is the short list.

  • Vendasta rebuilt its pricing. We said $42 to $999 per month. Every tier is now a $0 subscription set against a monthly spend minimum, and white-label starts at the $499 tier, not the cheapest one.
  • ClickFunnels has four tiers, not two. We listed "Startup $97 and Pro $297" and had missed the $197 plan, the annual prices and the $5,997 a year top tier.
  • HubSpot is cheaper to start than we said, $7 per seat per month on annual billing rather than the $20 monthly price we quoted. We had also never mentioned its required one-time onboarding fee.
  • Keap is now a Thryv brand, and we have removed an unverified implementation-fee range we should not have published.
  • ActiveCampaign, Systeme.io and GoHighLevel's own plans held exactly.

We did not re-rank anything. Two corrections favour competitors and the order still did not move, because the ranking here is by job and no job changed hands. A cheaper HubSpot entry seat is still a seat on a platform you cannot resell.

1. HubSpot, for teams that want polish over resale

HubSpot is the most polished CRM and marketing platform on this list, with the deepest reporting and the largest app ecosystem. It is the natural pick for a funded in-house team that values a clean interface and serious analytics more than reselling software.

  • Pricing (verified July 28, 2026): a free tier for up to 2 users, then Starter at $7 per seat per month on annual billing or $20 monthly, with 1,000 marketing contacts. Marketing Hub Professional is $800 per month billed annually or $890 monthly, including 3 Core Seats and 2,000 marketing contacts, with extra seats from $45. Enterprise is $3,600 per month with 5 Core Seats and 10,000 contacts.
  • The fee nobody quotes you: onboarding is required and one-time, $3,000 on Professional and $7,000 on Enterprise, on top of every monthly figure above. Contact tiers are sticky too: you cannot downgrade your paid tier until your contract renews.
  • The catch: there is no way to white-label or resell HubSpot, and the price scales steeply with contacts and seats. A single Professional subscription plus its required onboarding is more than a full year of GoHighLevel Agency Pro, which is why agencies rarely switch to it. For in-house teams with a budget and a reporting culture, that trade is often worth it.

2. ActiveCampaign, for email-first automation

If most of what you want from GoHighLevel is email and marketing automation with a light CRM attached, ActiveCampaign does that one job better and cheaper. Its automation builder is widely considered best in class.

  • Pricing (verified July 28, 2026, unchanged): at 1,000 contacts on annual billing, Starter $15, Plus $49, Pro $79 and Enterprise $145 per month, all rising with your contact count. There is no free plan, but there is a 14-day trial and a 30-day money-back guarantee. WhatsApp is now sold as its own plan family, with an email-plus-WhatsApp bundle.
  • The catch: it is not an all-in-one, and the entry plan is thinner than the price suggests. Pipelines and sales engagement are paid CRM add-ons, SMS and WhatsApp are add-ons, Starter is capped at one user and five actions per automation, and Pro includes three users. There is no funnel builder, no phone system and no resale mode. Costs also creep up as your list grows.

3. Systeme.io, the cheap all-in-one for solopreneurs

Systeme.io is the closest thing to a free GoHighLevel for one person. It bundles funnels, email, courses, and a blog into one simple tool, and the free plan is genuinely usable rather than a teaser.

  • Pricing (verified July 28, 2026, unchanged): free for up to 2,000 contacts, 3 funnels and 1 course, then Startup $17 per month for 5,000 contacts, Webinar $47 for 10,000, and Unlimited $97 for unlimited contacts plus sub-accounts and a free migration. Annual billing adds two free months. Every plan, including the free one, includes unlimited email sends, unlimited students and zero transaction fees.
  • The catch: it is built for solo creators, not agencies. The CRM and automation are lighter than GoHighLevel's, the design tools are basic, and there is no real white-label resale model.

4. Keap, for small service businesses

Keap (formerly Infusionsoft, and since acquired by Thryv, which now brands it "Keap, A Thryv, Inc. Brand") targets small service businesses that want strong automation plus hands-on help getting set up. It pairs a solid CRM and automation engine with guided onboarding.

  • Pricing (verified July 28, 2026): one unified plan, $299 per month month-to-month or $2,988 a year, which works out to $249 per month. Two users are included and extra users are $39 each, with contact pricing tiered above the starting allowance. An implementation package is required, but Keap does not publish its price, so get that number in writing before you sign.
  • Two costs to plan for: texting is metered much like GoHighLevel's wallet, with 500 messages and 100 voice minutes included and tiers from $24 to $279 a month above that. And an annual contract carries a $299 early termination fee.
  • The catch: the entry price is more than double GoHighLevel Starter before implementation is added, the mandatory package stings, and there is no white-label or resale option for agencies. What you are buying is the hand-holding, and for a small service business with nobody technical, that can genuinely be the right purchase.

5. Vendasta, the other agency white-label platform

Vendasta is the alternative most often compared with GoHighLevel for agencies, because it is also built around reselling under your own brand. The difference is the model: Vendasta is a marketplace where you resell other companies' products, while GoHighLevel rebrands one platform you operate yourself.

  • Pricing (rebuilt since we first published, verified July 28, 2026): the platform subscription is now $0 on every tier, set against a monthly wholesale spend minimum: Starter $99 (1 seat, no contract), Professional $499 (5 seats, one-year contract) and Premium $999 (10 seats, one-year contract). You pay the platform fee at signing to cover month one, then each $1 of qualifying product spend cancels $1 of subscription. Extra seats run $30 to $65, and client accounts and client users are unlimited.
  • The number that decides it: the white-label client portal starts at the $499 Professional tier. Starter is co-branded with Vendasta, so the cheapest way in is not a white-label way in.
  • The catch: the $0 subscription is real but it is not free, because the minimum spend is a floor you commit to whether or not you sell it on. Your cost of goods grows with every client, which is the opposite of GoHighLevel, where a flat $497 per month gets cheaper per client the more you add. Vendasta suits agencies that want a product catalog to resell and a fulfilment team behind it; GoHighLevel suits agencies that want to do the marketing work and own the platform.

6. ClickFunnels, for funnel-first marketers

ClickFunnels is the pick if your whole business runs on sales funnels and you do not need a full CRM or multi-client agency tooling. It is focused and good at the one thing it does.

  • Pricing (corrected July 28, 2026): four tiers, not two. Launch $97 a month or $81 annual (1 workspace, 10,000 contacts, 3 courses), Scale $197 or $164 (5 workspaces, 75,000 contacts), Optimize $297 or $248 (10 workspaces, 150,000 contacts), and an annual-only Dominate plan at $5,997 a year. All bundle courses, a website builder, email and unlimited funnels, with a 14-day trial and a 30-day money-back guarantee.
  • The gate that catches people: the $97 Launch plan that appears to price-match GoHighLevel Starter has no automations, no webhooks or API access, no appointments and a single CRM pipeline. Those start at Scale, $197. Compare Scale to GoHighLevel, not Launch.
  • The catch: it is funnel-first, not agency-first. There is no white-label resale, the CRM is thinner, and once you need multi-client management you outgrow it.

The 2026 question is not who has AI, it is how the AI is metered

Every platform on this list can claim AI. The difference that lands on your invoice is where the meter sits, and it is the thing most comparison posts skip.

  • Per sub-account: GoHighLevel meters AI Employee at $50 or $97 per sub-account per month. Ten clients means ten line items, not one.
  • Per plan tier: ActiveCampaign gives Starter and Plus limited access to Active Intelligence, and unlimited access only on Pro and Enterprise.
  • Per word quota: ClickFunnels grants 1 million AI words on Launch, rising to 10 million on Dominate.
  • As a separate product: HubSpot sells an answer-engine tracker, AEO, at $50 a month to follow 25 prompts across ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity, and meters other AI through credits, 3,000 on Professional and 5,000 on Enterprise.
  • Per client location: Vendasta bills its AI Workforce packages per location, so cost scales with your client roster rather than your team.

The practical test before you sign: ask the vendor to price your AI usage at ten clients, not one. Per-sub-account and per-location meters look cheap at one client and are the largest line on the invoice at twenty. You can start a GoHighLevel trial and price the sub-account math against your own client count.

When GoHighLevel is still the right call

After comparing all six, the honest conclusion is that most of these alternatives win on a single dimension (price, polish, or simplicity), but none replaces GoHighLevel for its core audience. GoHighLevel is still the right call if you:

  • Run an agency and want to resell software. The $497 SaaS Mode plan lets you rebrand the entire platform and sell it to clients on recurring subscriptions. Your cost stays flat while your client revenue grows, so margins expand as you scale, which is the opposite of a reseller marketplace.
  • Want to replace a stack of tools. One platform covers CRM, funnels, email, SMS, calendars, automation, reputation, and courses, so you cancel five or six separate subscriptions.
  • Serve multiple clients. Unlimited sub-accounts on the $297 plan keep each client cleanly separated.

If that sounds like you, the math usually favors GoHighLevel from the second or third resold client onward. You can start a free GoHighLevel trial here and test it before you commit. If you would rather not learn it yourself, our team offers done-for-you GoHighLevel setup and management, and you can also hire a dedicated GoHighLevel developer to build out your snapshots and automations.

The verdict

There is no single best GoHighLevel alternative, only the right tool for your situation. Pick HubSpot for polish, ActiveCampaign for email automation, Systeme.io if you are a solo creator on a budget, Keap for guided small-business automation, Vendasta if you want a reseller marketplace, and ClickFunnels if funnels are your whole game. But if you are an agency that wants to own and resell one all-in-one platform, GoHighLevel remains the strongest choice in 2026, and the usage costs and learning curve are a fair trade for what it replaces. Nothing in this July re-check moved that conclusion, including the two corrections that went in a competitor's favour. Want help deciding or setting it up? faqs: What is the best free alternative to GoHighLevel?

Systeme.io is the best genuinely free alternative. Its free plan covers up to 2,000 contacts, 3 sales funnels, a course, and a blog, which is enough for a solo creator to launch. The trade-off is a lighter CRM and automation than GoHighLevel and no white-label resale, so it fits individuals rather than agencies.
Is there a cheaper alternative to GoHighLevel?

Yes, if you only need part of what GoHighLevel does. Systeme.io starts at $17 per month and ActiveCampaign at $15 per month for 1,000 contacts on annual billing, both verified July 28, 2026. HubSpot Starter is cheaper still at $7 per seat per month annual, but it is a seat price, not a platform price. For a true all-in-one you can resell, GoHighLevel's $97 to $497 plans are hard to beat, just remember email, SMS, phone and AI usage are billed on top.
What is the best GoHighLevel alternative for agencies?

Vendasta is the closest white-label competitor, but check the tier before you compare prices: its white-label client portal starts at the $499 per month spend minimum, and the $99 Starter tier is co-branded with Vendasta. Vendasta also charges a $0 platform subscription against a monthly wholesale spend minimum, so your cost of goods rises with every client you add. GoHighLevel's flat $497 SaaS Mode plan gets cheaper per client as you scale, which is why most agencies that want to resell software still choose it.
GoHighLevel vs HubSpot, which is better?

They serve different buyers. HubSpot wins on polish, reporting and its app ecosystem for funded in-house teams. Verified July 28, 2026, Marketing Hub Professional is $800 per month billed annually or $890 monthly with 3 seats and 2,000 marketing contacts, plus a required one-time $3,000 onboarding fee. GoHighLevel wins on price and white-label resale for agencies. At agency scale HubSpot can cost roughly ten times more, which is why agencies rarely pick it.
Does GoHighLevel have a free trial?

Yes. All GoHighLevel plans include a 14-day free trial with no credit card required, and you can sometimes find extended 30-day trials through official promotions. Annual billing saves about 17 percent versus paying monthly.
Which GoHighLevel alternative is best for course creators?

Systeme.io is the best fit for most course creators because it bundles courses, funnels and email with a genuinely free starting tier, and every plan includes unlimited students and no transaction fees. ClickFunnels also handles courses well if sales funnels are central to your business, though its $97 Launch plan caps you at 3 courses and has no automations. GoHighLevel can host courses too, but it is usually overkill for a solo creator.
